independence.limitations: Shared workspace and agent environment; supplied network capture rather than independent acquisition. Author separation is sufficient for this documentary review, not a different organization/model, human endorsement, principal isolation or B09 closure. Main executor cannot alter this verdict.

snapshot.hashMeaning: SHA256 of exact file bytes without JSON or newline normalization.
snapshot.scope: Fresh AGENTS.md, documentation contract and bounded default context; relevant RF009-RF012 delivery, source, provenance, qualification and CAS records; frozen RF013 policy, source projection, ledger and capture helper.
snapshot.boundary: Baseline hashes identify reviewed entry bytes. RF013 hashes identify final frozen evidence after requested ordering and semantic clarifications. Subsequent integration prose is outside this snapshot.

optionEvaluation.candidate: sigstore@5.0.0 with proposed @sigstore/verify@4.1.2 and @sigstore/tuf@5.0.0 dependencies; exact SRI and gitHead values are bound in the reviewed policy.
optionEvaluation.npmNative: npm@12.0.2 documents audit signatures for downloaded packages and a verified JSON array. Detached-only invocation, complete signature failure semantics and bounded endpoint behavior are not established. Not selected.
optionEvaluation.pacote: pacote@22.0.0 documents manifest verification but verifies signatures and attestations only if present. Registry-scoped keys and TUF cache are required; tarball stream callbacks may repeat through retries. Not selected.
optionEvaluation.sigstore: Official maintained library documents detached DSSE verification without artifact bytes, issuer/URI/OID checks, log thresholds and public-key selection. Its API fits this bounded purpose best, but the exact closed configuration remains unqualified.
optionEvaluation.sigstoreCli: Official project identifies @sigstore/cli separately. Its exact version, integrity and interface were not established; the selected library is not a silently substituted CLI.
optionEvaluation.pinGap: Observed top-level versions/SRI are candidate identifiers, not authenticated installed artifacts. No closed transitive lock, authenticated Node pin, bootstrap-root digest or validated target snapshot exists. Dependency ranges cannot qualify the stack.
optionEvaluation.platformGap: Selected manifests require Node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0. Previously observed Windows Node 22.13.0 is insufficient. WSL Node availability and supported execution environment were not inspected or proven.

questions.question: Can standard verification precede the candidate download?
questions.finding: Yes in principle: documented verify accepts an attestation bundle without external artifact bytes. RF012 retained only a projection, omitting complete bundle fields. Supported bundle/Rekor combinations and exact complete input remain unproven; missing fields must not be fabricated.

questions.question: Is trust bootstrap and refresh sufficiently specified?
questions.finding: No. The embedded @sigstore/tuf bootstrap is a coherent route only after authenticating its toolchain and exact bytes. Required root/metadata/target versions, hashes, expiry and npm publish-key authority are missing. A bundle hint cannot authorize its own key. forceCache permits downloads when cache metadata expires and cannot enforce offline operation.

questions.question: Are exact identity and publisher semantics defined?
questions.finding: The revised candidate policy adequately states exact package/SHA512, one subject and one required statement of each type, repository/workflow/ref/commit, issuer, numeric repository/owner IDs, push event, builder, invocation and resolved dependency. URI matching must escape regex characters and anchor both ends; email override is forbidden. The npm publish assertion does not identify an npm user. These are required checks, not authenticated results.

questions.question: Are certificate, transparency and historical-time guarantees established?
questions.finding: No. Chain/EKU/SCT, checkpoint/inclusion/shard semantics, authenticated signing time, historical validity, root/key validity and replay/freshness policy must be enforced by the maintained verifier. README thresholds alone do not prove those exact guarantees. Consistency/witness acceptance, finite receipt expiry and exact failure handling remain unresolved. No custom cryptographic fallback is permissible.

questions.question: Are source-version and input compatibility claims sufficiently evidenced?
questions.finding: No. The verify README was captured at the client gitHead while proposed verify@4.1.2 declares a different gitHead. The compatibility table values were not retained. Exact configuration/source checks are needed before asserting support for the candidate bundles.

questions.question: Are network, cache, failure and hooks controlled?
questions.finding: Only as candidate requirements. Separate online refresh with exact enumerated paths and cumulative limits, private cache, enforced offline verification, zero retries and failure normalization require qualification. Documented keySelector is a hook for accepted pinned keys, not arbitrary retrieval. No sign/attest, installer, lifecycle, ambient cache or payload-fetch fallback is admitted.

questions.question: Does the proposed quarantine cap establish acquisition readiness?
questions.finding: No. 536870912 bytes is an administrative ceiling, not measured compressed size or authenticated publisher size. Capacity, reserve, duration, owned staging and parser bounds are absent. Standard provenance must pass before download; whole-archive integrity must pass before parsing. Native hashes require bounded decompression and remain derived evidence.

questions.question: Is the receipt an implemented admission schema?
questions.finding: No. It lists required fields and denial intent; executable field typing, exact accepted result shapes and configuration qualification remain open. Neither a library return value nor RF012 partial mathematics grants admission.

networkReview.limitation: Offline arithmetic and projection-to-ledger agreement establish recorded accounting only; full response retention and production transport enforcement were not independently verified.

contractDecision.phaseA: Non-operative proposal: authenticate exact package digest and authorized publisher/build identity through the qualified standard mechanism, then bind separate finite acquisition authority.
contractDecision.phaseB: Non-operative proposal: bounded inert download, complete archive digest verification before any parser, then bounded static inspection and derived native inventory before extraction or placement.
contractDecision.splitCondition: Any operative split must independently revise all coupled manifest, authority, download, stage and acceptance clauses. Unknown published compressed size and member identity cannot be silently waived.
contractDecision.qualification: D01-D06 remain blocked; B01-B09 remain open. This review does not qualify a package, binary, WSL environment, schema, containment or runtime.
